growth_signal.value: Valuation jumped to $14.6 billion in a Nvidia-backed round in March 2026, then it raised $3.36 billion more and filed to go public on the NYSE just six months later.

raised.value: $3.36B in pre-IPO financing (September 2026), on top of earlier rounds including $2B plus a $900M credit line

entry.idea: AI companies need huge amounts of computing power, but building and running the data centers, power supply and cooling for that is slow and expensive, so Nscale builds and runs full AI data centers, from power to software, and rents that capacity out.
entry.lesson: When everyone needs a scarce physical resource to build a hot new technology, building that infrastructure can be a bigger business than building on top of it.
entry.name: Nscale

growth.reason: Its valuation and funding have grown enormously within a year, from a $14.6B round to a $3.36B raise ahead of an IPO, plus a $1.65B acquisition.

market.reason: Almost every AI company and large enterprise in the world needs the computing power Nscale sells.

tech.reason: It uses existing GPU and data-center technology; its edge is speed of execution, capital and partnerships like Nvidia rather than new science.

entry.twist: It owns the whole stack itself, from energy supply and data center buildings to the cloud software on top, instead of just reselling other companies' hardware or power.
entry.who_pays: AI labs and large companies pay to rent GPU computing power and cloud services from Nscale.
entry.why_now: The rush to build and run large AI models has created a worldwide shortage of data center and computing capacity that only new large-scale builders can fill.
